messages:
alex: Heads up — bumped Gemma-13B through our converter this morning and the roundtrip tokenizer check shows two tokens collapsing into one (seen in logits + final text). model run: gemma-13b -> redwood-format. short repro attached below.

priya: ugh. can you paste a tiny example of input vs output? sample tokens?

alex: sure — input: "In the middle of the night" -> token ids: [425, 11, 2049...]. after conversion+load: text becomes "Inthe middle of thenight" (tokens merged). small dump: ```orig_ids: [425,11,2049,77]
conv_ids: [425,2049,77]```

matt: my 1st guess is vocab aliasing + tokenizer normalization mismatch. also possible rotary/headwise mapping mismatch that shifts decoding boundary making tokenizer emit different merges. did we change endianness or byte-order during conversion?

alex: no explicit endianness touched, but converter uses a fast path that flattens vocab into a single byte-level map. i ran tokenizer roundtrip script and saw 1.2% token-level disagreement on the QA bench, +3.4% ppl regression.

ci-bot: conversion-job/421: failed QC: token-discrepancy > threshold (count=3). logs: https://ci/redwood/conv/421 (truncated)

priya: ok two actionable forks: (A) run tokenizer-normalizer (NFKC) + roundtrip on a large sample and diff hash of vocab -> see if string normalization changed; (B) compare raw byte sequence of vocab file before/after conversion (sha256). alex can you grab the two shas?

alex: sha256s: orig_vocab: ab12f3... conv_vocab: ab12f3... (same) but when i dump the token bytes there are two entries where the byte sequences differ by a leading 0x00. e.g. orig token: [0xE2,0x80,0x99] conv token: [0x00,0xE2,0x80,0x99]. so looks like an accidental padding insertion.

matt: that would definitely cause merges in BPE postprocess. if token bytes shift, BPE merges might produce different merges — especially if the padding produces a join. how did padding get introduced? maybe a C layer struct alignment bug in the converter.

sarah: also check rotary params: if head-dim ordering changed some tokens end up with different kv cache indices which can surface as subtle decoding diffs under int4. can someone run the per-head rotary-check that prints headwise checksum? quick script: ```python -c "print(sum(np.abs(rotary_matrix).sum(axis=(1,2))))"```

alex: ran headwise checks. per-head checksum diffs at head 0 and 7 only (small but > tol). when i run float16 model (no quant) the text mismatch still appears but quieter. with int4 quant the merge happens more often.

priya: that suggests two problems compounding: a token-byte padding bug in converter + a headwise rotary permutation difference that amplifies probs under quantization. we should revert the fast-path and retest on a non-flattened conversion pipeline for a sanity run.

matt: i'll bisect the converter commit range. assigning myself. will run hexdump diff on vocab and a minimal C-struct layout test to catch alignment/padding.

alex: i'll run the tokenizer roundtrip over the 10k sample and produce token-diff freq table. leaving quantization off for now. expected results by EOD.

priya: i'll re-run eval harness (QA + summarization sets) on float16 to get baseline numbers. put results in /tmp/gemma-onboard/bench-FP16.txt and tag this thread. :+1:

ci-bot: job/convert-fastpath-revert triggered by matt — build 745 queued.

sarah: once we have the clean conversion, also run the rotary-head-reorder test with a known good llm-runtime kernel (kernel-v12) to ensure KV cache indexing stable across load paths. i've seen similar headwise reorders when reshaping weight tensors with wrong stride assumptions.

alex: noted — will add that to the checklist. thanks all, will post diffs and the token-diff CSV here when ready.

matt: FYI if anyone hits this locally, quick local check: ```python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('vocab.json'); print(t.encode('In the middle of the night').ids)"``` — compare before/after. saves time. :mag:
